title: Ἱππιατρικά — Hippiatrica (Corpus Hippiatricorum Graecorum); RU: «Гиппиатрика». Proposed unit: Apsyrtus' excerpts
author: Compilation: Apsyrtus, Hierocles, Theomnestus, Eumelus, Pelagonius (in Greek), Anatolius and others
date: Sources 3rd–5th c. CE; late-antique compilation, recensions down to 10th c.
size: Oder–Hoppe CHG I–II, c. 800 Teubner pp.; est. 200k+ words across recensions
edition: Oder & Hoppe, Corpus Hippiatricorum Graecorum I–II, Leipzig 1924–27 (public domain in the US by date; EU status depends on the editors' death dates).
ru_evidence: ru.wikipedia «Гиппиатрика» (derived from the English article) cites no translation; none found in the checked Russian catalogues.
en_evidence: No complete translation. McCabe, A Byzantine Encyclopaedia of Horse Medicine (OUP 2007) translates excerpts only; en.wikipedia lists no translation.
other_translations: No complete modern translation found in any language.
value: Unique ancient veterinary corpus. Apsyrtus served with the army on the Danube; his letters to named soldiers and landowners illuminate army logistics, horse-breeding and rural society. Also charms, verse and proverbs. For historians of medicine, the Roman army, agriculture and compilation.
ai_feasibility: medium: practical prose and letters; risks are hippological and drug terms and parallel recensions. A good showcase for visible agent debate over variants.
pilot_unit: Apsyrtus' prefaces and letters plus the opening fever chapters of the Berlin recension (CHG I), est. 8–10k words
